title.value: Automate daily post checks and publishing logic

introduction.value: A Zapier agent watches for a post with today's date, checks whether it was already posted, analyzes the copy, and uses Zapier Tables.

method.value: The poster had been trying to build a Zap that pulled scheduled LinkedIn copy from a Zapier Table fed by an interface and published it on the right day. Their colleague replaced the Scheduler -> Table -> LinkedIn Zap with an agent instructed to find a record whose calendar date matched the current date, confirm it had not already been posted, extract the copy, and send it to LinkedIn while preserving line breaks and emojis.

outcome.value: It worked much faster to set up than the original Zap attempt: the poster says they spent hours on the Zap, while the colleague built the agent in about 15 minutes. The main issue the agent solved was formatting preservation for emojis and line breaks, which had been the sticking point in the Zap.

notes.value: The clearest catch was formatting: the original Zap struggled with emojis and line breaks from the table, so the agent needed an explicit instruction to preserve the copy exactly.

source_text.body:
Automate daily post checks and publishing logic
A Zapier agent watches for a post with today's date, checks whether it was already posted, analyzes the copy, and uses Zapier Tables.
Done with
ZA
Zapier Agents
What they did
The poster had been trying to build a Zap that pulled scheduled LinkedIn copy from a Zapier Table fed by an interface and published it on the right day. Their colleague replaced the Scheduler -> Table -> LinkedIn Zap with an agent instructed to find a record whose calendar date matched the current date, confirm it had not already been posted, extract the copy, and send it to LinkedIn while preserving line breaks and emojis.
How it went
It worked much faster to set up than the original Zap attempt: the poster says they spent hours on the Zap, while the colleague built the agent in about 15 minutes. The main issue the agent solved was formatting preservation for emojis and line breaks, which had been the sticking point in the Zap.
Worth knowing
The clearest catch was formatting: the original Zap struggled with emojis and line breaks from the table, so the agent needed an explicit instruction to preserve the copy exactly.
Try it yourself
with
Zapier Agents
Copy prompt
Create a Zapier agent that checks [blog CMS / Google Sheet / Notion] each morning for a post dated today. It should look in a Zapier Table to see whether that post was already published, review the copy for [tone, length, or other rules], and record the result in the table. If it's new and passes, show me the post and ask for approval before publishing to [platform].
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/zapier/comments/1mf6cge/agent_embarrassment
